answers.explanation: 32 addresses minus the network and broadcast addresses: 30.
Two fewer prefix bits than /24 means 2² = 4 class C networks, 1,024 addresses.
One more network bit means one fewer host bit, so the block size halves and the subnet count doubles.
/20 is between /16 and /24, so the count is how many /20s fit in a class B: 2⁴ = 16.
2ʰ − 2: all the combinations of host bits, minus the all-0s network address and the all-1s broadcast.
200 is 11001000: a 1 after a 0. Partial octets can only be 128, 192, 224, 240, 248, 252, 254, or 255.
